# Heavy metal contamination in rice

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="rice-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="rice-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="rice-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Rice metal levels depend on growing conditions, grain form and preparation ([[sources/seyfferth2025-rice-water-management-as-hg-cd]] [[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]] [[sources/carey2015-rice-arsenic-percolating-cooking]]). Water management can trade lower inorganic arsenic for higher cadmium ([[sources/seyfferth2025-rice-water-management-as-hg-cd]] [[sources/limmer2026-arkansas-rice-water-management]]).

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Inorganic arsenic and cadmium are central concerns ([[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]). Lead, total mercury and chromium are also measured; chemical species remain separate ([[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]).

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Soil, cultivar and water management influence uptake ([[sources/seyfferth2025-rice-water-management-as-hg-cd]]). Bran retention, milling and cooking change the rice material being compared ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]] [[sources/carey2015-rice-arsenic-percolating-cooking]]).

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Compare the same arsenic species and rice preparation ([[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]). Check arsenic and cadmium together when changing origin, irrigation or processing, then verify the delivered lot ([[sources/seyfferth2025-rice-water-management-as-hg-cd]] [[sources/limmer2026-arkansas-rice-water-management]]).

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="direct-answer"></a>
<a id="overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Rice overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>

Use this review to compare a rice result with the available occurrence evidence, investigate sourcing differences and select controls to verify. The profile covers inorganic and total arsenic, cadmium, lead, nickel, chromium and mercury where measurements are available ([[sources/carey2020-global-low-ias-rice-sourcing]] [[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]] [[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]). Grain, cooked rice and derived foods retain their own measurement bases ([[sources/carey2020-global-low-ias-rice-sourcing]] [[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]] [[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]).

<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>

The most consequential control decision is often the joint response of arsenic and cadmium: a water regime that lowers one can raise the other, while some field settings show lower arsenic without a statistically detected cadmium increase ([[sources/seyfferth2025-rice-water-management-as-hg-cd]] [[sources/limmer2026-arkansas-rice-water-management]]). The evidence below identifies where that distinction changes a sourcing or processing decision.

<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## Rice identity and scope

<a id="grain-fractions-and-derived-ingredients"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>

This page covers edible brown, white and cooked rice. Brown rice retains the bran and germ; polishing removes outer tissues ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]]). Flour, bran, syrup, protein ingredients and drinks have separate processing and composition evidence ([[sources/jackson2012-arsenic-organic-foods-brown-rice-syrup]]). Uncooked grain describes a food form; dry weight describes an analytical moisture basis ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]]).

<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

Use published concentrations as context for your laboratory result. Match the measurement and reference below. A reference made from study summaries does not establish a percentile for an individual lot ([[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]).

## Heavy metal contamination profile of rice

<a id="chemical-species-and-measurement-basis"></a>
<a id="arsenic-species-across-market-rice"></a>
<a id="cadmium-and-other-elements"></a>
<a id="mercury-species"></a>
<a id="prepared-food-observations"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-007"></a>
<a id="which-metals-and-chemical-species-have-been-investigated-in-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-008"></a>
<a id="what-concentrations-detection-frequencies-and-variability-were-observed-in-each-defined-sampling-frame"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-009"></a>
<a id="which-analyte-questions-are-unassessed-access-blocked-conflicting-or-searched-without-eligible-evidence"></a>
<a id="arsenic-species-and-occurrence-evidence"></a>
<a id="sampling-censoring-and-shared-observations"></a>
<a id="mercury-species-and-comparison-boundaries"></a>

Compare source-reported findings across rice types, collection regions and periods. Low, Moderate and High show each finding’s position against a scoped HMI baseline; they are concentration comparisons, not safety or certainty grades. Different arsenic species and preparation bases remain separate. Open a result for its reference, methods and limitations, or use the information button beside this heading for the comparison methods and scope.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-rice" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-rice-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

HMI pools compatible evidence across sampling families to calculate fixed rice references. The dry-grain references combine FDA category medians with Carey regional medians for inorganic arsenic and DMA, FDA with Myanmar township medians for total arsenic, and Myanmar with Shi country medians for cadmium ([[sources/carey2020-global-low-ias-rice-sourcing]] [[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]] [[sources/myatsoe2023-myanmar-rice-metals]] [[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling]]). Native-moisture references combine Saudi and Myanmar grain evidence using the Myanmar study’s measured 6–7% moisture loss ([[sources/myatsoe2023-myanmar-rice-metals]] [[sources/alrashdi2024-rice-ias-cd-pb-hg-saudi-arabia]]). Each family receives equal weight; its subgroups share that weight. These references describe subgroup medians in the evidence library, not the median of all rice sold worldwide. Each row’s reported mean or median is compared with that reference; means are never relabelled as medians. Cooked rice remains separate. Low is below Q1, Moderate is Q1–Q3, and High is above Q3; reporting bounds must support one position. The sidebar shows contributing families, conversions, count-weighted and leave-one-family-out sensitivity, and the limitations of single-family references. These are concentration positions, not safety or certainty grades.

<p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Arsenic species and occurrence evidence</p>

Rice occurrence studies cover different chemical species, grain forms and sampling frames ([[sources/carey2020-global-low-ias-rice-sourcing]] [[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]] [[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]]). The table brings international surveys, field-grown grain, commercial rice products and FDA cooked-rice composites together by analyte, while retaining each source’s reported statistic and measurement basis. A mean, median and detected range answer different questions; the table labels each explicitly.

EFSA’s 2024 organoarsenic assessment adds a separate evidence stream. Its occurrence analysis includes DMA measurements in polished and brown grain, while some processed-food estimates are derived using recipes and an assumption of no processing loss ([[sources/efsa2024-organoarsenic-species]]). Direct grain observations and model-derived flour, porridge or beverage values must remain distinguishable ([[sources/efsa2024-organoarsenic-species]]). Organic arsenic is not one interchangeable substance with one toxicological interpretation ([[sources/efsa2024-organoarsenic-species]]).

<p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sampling, censoring and shared observations</p>

Sampling and censoring matter as much as the reported concentration. The global cadmium compilation reuses earlier studies and substitutes half the detection limit for low results ([[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]]). The Henan monitoring summaries also include substituted non-detects ([[sources/yan2025-rice-heavy-metals-henan-china]]). Their reported medians remain usable source summaries, but they are not medians of detected samples and cannot supply a matched trend against the FDA composites ([[sources/shi2020-rice-grain-cadmium-global-supply-chain]] [[sources/yan2025-rice-heavy-metals-henan-china]]).

Source rows preserve the counted unit. The Vietnamese field study covers genotypes with paired brown and white grain; the Ethiopian study combines farmers’ grain into area composites ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]] [[sources/desalew2023-rice-ethiopia]]). Multiple analyte rows reuse those same materials ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]] [[sources/desalew2023-rice-ethiopia]]). Neither more rows nor technical repeats create additional independent studies ([[sources/tran2024-arsenic-cadmium-vietnamese-rice-qtl]] [[sources/desalew2023-rice-ethiopia]]).

<p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Mercury species and comparison boundaries</p>

Direct mercury measurements remain separate from model outputs. Brombach’s European survey reports both total mercury and methylmercury in a mixture of grain and rice products; its overall range cannot be assigned to a grain-only or baby-food subgroup ([[sources/brombach2017-methylmercury-european-commercial-rice]]). Cui’s spatial model addresses a different question and does not contribute a new measured product distribution to this table ([[sources/cui2022-mercury-speciation-rice-china]]).

Original source means, medians, ranges and measurement bases remain visible. Recovered individual measurements and regional summaries supply compatible HMI references; the baseline does not require every study to report a percentile. Unknown moisture bases and unresolved reporting limits remain explicit ([[sources/desalew2023-rice-ethiopia]]). Neither below-LOQ results nor an absence of detections establishes zero contamination ([[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020]] [[sources/desalew2023-rice-ethiopia]]).

Median of selected cooked-food composites: 43 µg/kg. HMI median 55; Q1 43; Q3 66 µg/kg. 1 family. Not a safety grade.</p><p>Low is below Q1; Moderate includes Q1 through Q3; High is above Q3. Reporting bounds must give the same category throughout.</p><p>This finding’s sampling family contributes to the fixed reference.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sensitivity to weighting</p><p>Equal rice-form weight instead of equal composite weight: Moderate. The position is unchanged under this alternative. This check does not address all sampling, rounding or analytical uncertainty.</p><div data-baseline-reference="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-cooked-tAs:fe2a86fa5481"><a href="#hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-cooked-tAs:fe2a86fa5481">Reference, contributing evidence and methods</a></div></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Year-by-year source results</p><p class="hmi-scope-note" data-timeline-scope>All collection regions; all available source years.</p><div data-selected-timeline><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal year</th><th scope="col">Samples</th><th scope="col">Detected</th><th scope="col">Sample median (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Detected range (µg/kg)</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018</td><td>12</td><td>12/12</td><td>41.5</td><td>26–62</td></tr><tr><td>FY2019</td><td>9</td><td>9/9</td><td>45</td><td>20–75</td></tr><tr><td>FY2020</td><td>6</td><td>6/6</td><td>49.5</td><td>29–69</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Collection regions</p><p class="hmi-scope-note" data-regional-scope>All source years in all sampled regions.</p><div data-selected-regional><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Collection region</th><th scope="col">Composites</th><th scope="col">Detected</th><th scope="col">Sample median (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Detected range (µg/kg)</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Mid-Atlantic</td><td>4</td><td>4/4</td><td>50.5</td><td>41–55</td></tr><tr><td>North Central</td><td>4</td><td>4/4</td><td>43</td><td>20–69</td></tr><tr><td>Northeast</td><td>5</td><td>5/5</td><td>43</td><td>40–62</td></tr><tr><td>Southeast</td><td>5</td><td>5/5</td><td>32</td><td>29–53</td></tr><tr><td>Southwest</td><td>4</td><td>4/4</td><td>54.5</td><td>42–75</td></tr><tr><td>West</td><td>5</td><td>5/5</td><td>35</td><td>26–45</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div><p>FDA TDS prepared-food composite in the stated cooked form; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>55</td><td>CSV source row 8331; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>56</td><td>CSV source row 56190; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>5.6</td><td>CSV source row 8332; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>13</td><td>CSV source row 56191; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;50</td><td>CSV source row 8319; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;50</td><td>CSV source row 56178; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;4</td><td>CSV source row 8333; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;4</td><td>CSV source row 56192; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;1</td><td>CSV source row 8334; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;1</td><td>CSV source row 56193; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;40</td><td>CSV source row 8335; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>65</td><td>CSV source row 56194; We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. (2020): Moderate.</li></ul><p>These checks show dependence on each sampling family; they are not confidence intervals.</p><div data-baseline-reference="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-pooled-dry-iAs:e27e8c1757aa"><a href="#hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-pooled-dry-iAs:e27e8c1757aa">Reference, contributing evidence and methods</a></div></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Collection period</p><p data-timeline-scope>2012–2013 release</p><div data-selected-timeline><p>No year-by-year sample register is reconstructed from this summary.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Geographic scope</p><p data-regional-scope>United States · retail survey</p><div data-selected-regional><p>Purchase market; origins and processing differ by category.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sampling, analysis and reporting limits</p><p>FDA arsenic speciation survey; summary category averages, including specified substitutions.</p><p>Summary averages use half total arsenic when samples were not speciated, and half the detection limit when total arsenic was below detection. Basmati and jasmine categories include both brown and white products; preparation also varies. FDA used substitutions for some non-speciated or non-detected samples. no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;1</td><td>CSV source row 8337; no moisture/basis conversion.</p><div data-shared-evidence-content><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>How the comparison is calculated</summary><p>Earlier matched collections uses the latest selected year and the earliest earlier year with common region × season groups. We calculate a median within each group, then the median across the same groups in each year, with equal group weight. Unmatched composites remain in the source tables. Other collection regions matches fiscal year and season and balances the peer regions. These are descriptive sample comparisons.</p><p>A reference middle 50% is the earlier groups' Q1–Q3, with linear interpolation. It describes that reference set; it is not a normal range, a safety threshold or an outlier test. A single earlier measurement has no meaningful reference distribution.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Sampling, analytical methods and reporting limits</summary><p>Regional results are prepared-food composites from collection markets, not growing origins or individual brands. Fiscal-year coverage is uneven. Matched comparisons retain common region/season strata, with equal stratum weight. Different sampled composites are not a longitudinal panel or a demonstrated population trend.</p><p>FDA regional foods combine purchases from three cities into one prepared-food composite. Row-specific administrative reporting limits are preserved. A non-detect is bounded by its reporting limit; no concentration is imputed. The multi-analyte rice records contain winter-only FY2020 collections; this does not mean every analyte was tested in that year. Matching also addresses unequal regional coverage, including the absence of West in the FY2018 winter subset.</p><p><a href="https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-total-diet-study-tds/fda-total-diet-study-tds-design-and-implementation">FDA collection and preparation design</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/media/159746/download?attachment=">Original data key</a></p><p>Unmatched source-year summaries describe every reported sample in that year. The selected comparison uses only its declared matching groups. Different fiscal years can include collections from the same calendar year.</p><p>Collection markets do not identify growing or ingredient origin. Other collection regions compares samples matched by year and season.</p><p>Source-value tables retain public category-level sample identifiers, fiscal year, reported result and original locator. A zero lower interval endpoint is never displayed as an observed concentration.</p></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source reuse limits</summary><p>Comparisons concern the selected historical dataset and are not current supplier rankings, compliance findings or independent measurements. They are descriptive sample comparisons and do not establish a population trend.</p></details></div><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Source values and extraction locators (27)</summary><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fiscal / calendar year</th><th scope="col">Region / season</th><th scope="col">Reported result (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Source locator</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FY2018 / CY2017</td><td>Mid-Atlantic / Winter</td><td>&lt;1</td><td>CSV source row 56196;
